rv.q: Daniel Bailey’s dynamic production pulses with the jazz played by Lyons, weaving music around the taut scenes.
Conviction and powerful authority are the hallmarks of every performance in this fizzing and compelling masterwork.
Headlong’s revival of Fences is impressively honed, with the simmering first act infusing significance into the explosive second.
Fences is an exceptional piece of drama that does what drama does best: it allows us to embrace complexity and nuance by letting us live a life through someone else’s eyes.

cn.t: Wilson's classic family drama receives a dynamic, compelling revival with outstanding performances and urgent relevance, though it remains a demanding three-hour exploration of masculinity and thwarted ambition in 1950s America.
